tasks.corrected_reference_answer: SecureCookieSession access methods mark accessed so save_session can add Vary: Cookie (src/flask/sessions.py:362-364). That flag does not determine serialization: should_set_cookie checks modified or permanent with SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST (259-261); only then does save_session dump/sign the session (383-387). Read-only permanent sessions may be refreshed by policy, but that cost is not caused by unconditionally setting accessed.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: copy_current_request_context captures ctx.copy once and runs the wrapped function under that context (src/flask/ctx.py:179-193). RequestContext.copy creates a new context object but shares the request, environ and current session (337-355). Context-local bindings are distinct, but mutable request/session data are not isolated; the docstring specifically warns that thread access to the shared request must be locked.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: _find_error_handler loops over at most two code categories, blueprint/app scopes, then exception MRO for nonempty maps, returning the first match (src/flask/sansio/app.py:831-846). A no-match worst case is O(B*M) dictionary lookups for B scopes and M MRO entries under usual dictionary assumptions. Handler count does not multiply this directly. Deep hierarchies can add work, but a measured bottleneck is not established, and reversing MRO would change specificity semantics. Caching would need keys and invalidation that preserve scope/code precedence.
